To speed up further allocations SLUB may store empty slabs in per cpu/node
partial lists instead of freeing them immediately.  This prevents per
memcg caches destruction
column2: because kmem caches created for a memory cgroup

column1: are only destroyed after the last page charged to the cgroup is freed.
To fix this issue
column2: this patch resurrects approach first proposed in [1].

column1: It forbids SLUB to cache empty slabs after the memory cgroup that the
cache belongs to was destroyed.  It is achieved by setting kmem_cache's
cpu_partial and min_partial constants to 0 and tuning put_cpu_partial() so
that it would drop frozen empty slabs immediately if cpu_partial = 0.
The runtime overhead is minimal.  From all the hot functions
touch relatively cold put_cpu_partial(): we make it call
unfreeze_partials() after freezing a slab that belongs to an offline
memory cgroup.  Since slab freezing exists to avoid moving slabs from/to a
partial list on free/alloc
column2: and there can't be allocations from dead

column1: caches
column2: it shouldn't cause any overhead.  We do have to disable preemption

column1: for put_cpu_partial() to achieve that though.
The original patch was accepted well and even merged to the mm tree.
However
column2: I decided to withdraw it due to changes happening to the memcg

column1: core at that time.  I had an idea of introducing per-memcg shrinkers for
kmem caches
column3: as memcg has finally settled down

column1: as an option
column2: because SLUB shrinker would be too costly to call since SLUB

column1: does not keep free slabs on a separate list.  Besides
even call per-memcg shrinkers for offline memcgs.  Overall
introduce much more complexity to both SLUB and memcg than this small
patch.
Regarding to SLAB
per-cpu/node caches periodically.  Thanks to list_lru reparenting
longer keep entries for offline cgroups in per-memcg arrays (such as
memcg_cache_params->memcg_caches)
column2: so we do not have to bother if a

column1: per-memcg cache will be shrunk a bit later than it could be.
